key_insight: CorDex can learn robust, functional dexterous grasps for novel objects using synthetic variations generated from a single human demonstration, by combining semantic and geometric reasoning into the training loop.
problem_solved: Overcomes the twin bottlenecks of limited large-scale dexterous-grasp datasets and the lack of models that jointly reason about object semantics and contact geometry, enabling functional tool-use grasps from minimal demonstration data.
method: Generate: synthesize diverse object/hand interaction examples from one human demonstration via procedural augmentation of poses, contacts, and object variants.
Transfer: map synthesized grasps to a robotic dexterous hand using kinematic/trajectory retargeting and sim-to-real strategies.
Adapt: refine policies with integrated semantic (task/context) and geometric (contact/shape) reasoning to generalize to novel objects and real-world noise.
impact: Reduces data-collection burden and speeds up deployment of dexterous manipulation by enabling few-shot learning of functional grasps, making it easier for AI/ML and robotics practitioners to teach robots new tool-use behaviors quickly.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: single human demo → synthetic augmentation → transfer to robot → real-world adaptation

paper_title: Generate, Transfer, Adapt: Learning Functional Dexterous Grasping from a Single Human Demonstration
paper_authors: Xingyi He, Adhitya Polavaram, Yunhao Cao, Om Deshmukh, Tianrui Wang
